data.bug_class: uncontrolled memory allocation (OOM) from attacker-controlled length; no out-of-bounds access found empirically
data.rationale: bam_hdr_read reads h->l_text straight from the BAM header (le_to_u32) and immediately mallocs h->l_text+1 bytes with no upper bound other than the 32-bit range, so a 4-byte field in an input reachable from hts_open/sam_hdr_read via LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput forces multi-GB allocations. Empirical evidence: ASan+libFuzzer runs of /out/hts_open_fuzzer seeded with the project's own test corpus (~2M execs, fork mode ignoring OOMs) produced no heap-buffer-overflow/UAF, but repeatedly aborted with out-of-memory reports whose stack is exactly bam_hdr_read sam.c:218 (e.g. malloc(3082270509) and malloc(4193845249)); matching artifacts were saved. A hand-crafted BAM attempting the CG-tag CIGAR relocation path (bam_tag2cigar, sam.c:479-514) was blocked by bam_aux_get/skip_aux validation (sam.c:3247-3304), so that path appears guarded in this tree. Confidence is moderate: fuzzing was time-limited and did not cover CRAM deeply; if the graded bug is a strict memory-safety violation, the next most likely candidates are the BAM record parser (bam_read1/bam_tag2cigar, sam.c:480-514) and VCF genotype parsing (vcf_parse_format, vcf.c ~2280-2420).
